title: As for me and my house (Joshua 24:15)
word: As for me and my house
hook: choose this day whom you'll serve

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rahab: a woman on the wall, a lie to the king's men, and a thread of hope in her window. Your line was the scarlet cord. Whose courage did you notice? Today, the last day of the road out of Egypt. Day three hundred ninety-one.

You've probably seen it on a wooden plaque by somebody's front door, or painted over a kitchen archway: as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. It's become a kind of household motto. But the line was first said by an old soldier at a tense public assembly, in front of every tribe of Israel, and it wasn't decoration. It was a dare. Joshua is near the end of his life. The land has been settled. And he calls everyone to a town called Shechem, because he's going to make them choose.
screen: `A PLAQUE BY THE FRONT DOOR.` → `FIRST, AN OLD SOLDIER'S DARE.` → `EVERYONE CALLED TO SHECHEM.`

segments.voice: First, the story retold. Before he asks anything, Joshua tells them the whole story, speaking for God: Abraham called from beyond the river, Jacob going down to Egypt, Moses and Aaron, the sea, the wilderness, a land you didn't work for, cities you didn't build, vineyards you didn't plant. Everything you have was given. Second, the choice. Then: if serving the Lord seems wrong to you, choose this day whom you will serve. The old gods your ancestors served, or the gods of the land you're living in. And then his own answer, before anyone else's: "but as for me and my house we will serve the Lord." He goes first, and he answers for his household, not the whole nation. Third, the surprise. The people shout: we'll serve the Lord too! And Joshua says something no one expects. You can't. He is a holy God, a jealous God. It's as if he wants them to feel the weight of it, not just say yes because everyone else is. And they say it again: no, we will serve the Lord. So he writes it down and sets up a great stone under an oak as a witness. Fourth, look back over the road. This part of the path began with two midwives who said no. Then a basket in the reeds, a bush that burned, a lamb and a sea, manna, Sinai and ten words, a golden calf, God's back, a blessing, a talking donkey, the Shema, choose life, Moses on Nebo, Rahab's cord. And it ends where Moses ended: with a choice that has to be made again. Catholics make it again every Easter, renewing their baptismal promises out loud.
screen: `A LAND YOU DIDN'T WORK FOR.` · `CHOOSE THIS DAY WHOM YOU'LL SERVE.` · `YOU CAN'T. HE IS HOLY.` · `A STONE UNDER THE OAK.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: choose again today. Settle, and breathe. Whatever you've chosen before, a faith, a marriage, a vocation, a sobriety, a promise to a friend, it doesn't run on autopilot. Joshua's people had chosen at Sinai. He still asked them again. Bring one of your big choices to mind. Look at it honestly, the way Joshua made them look: the weight of it, the cost. Then, if you can, choose it again, freshly, for today. If you pray, you can say Joshua's line as your own: as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. If you don't, simply renew the choice in your own words. The bell holds the time.
As for me and my house. Joshua's answer at Shechem: he chose first, for his own household, and dared the people to choose too. Today's word.
screen: `AS FOR ME AND MY HOUSE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: we will serve the lord. Today, choose one commitment again on purpose, and tell one person you live with. Tomorrow, new country: judges, kings, prophets, wisdom, and the seven books. Day three hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: At the Easter Vigil and on Easter Sunday, Catholics renew their baptismal promises aloud, rejecting sin and professing faith, and many Catholic families call their home a domestic church, a phrase the Catechism uses for the Christian household.

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice saying for a kitchen wall.
what it means: a public dare at the end of a long road: choose this day, and Joshua chooses first.
what a scholar hears: the Shechem covenant ceremony retells the history, demands a choice, and sets a witness stone, the shape of an ancient covenant renewal.
